description: Morphology-agnostic from-scratch sensorimotor adaptation. A fresh graph receives opaque actuator tokens and raw pose/contact/effort receipts, performs motor babble, learns graph-resident body-frame forward models, detects changed consequences through prediction error, adapts at fast and slow timescales, and predicts the next action toward a graph-held goal. Matched frozen-plasticity and no-learning controls are also graph-native.

microtheory.name: embodied_adaptation
microtheory.description: Learn what an unnamed body can do from intervention, track damage or wear as changed consequences without a fault label, then choose by forward prediction rather than imported kinematics.

rules.name: ea_measure_goal_state
rules.comment: Distance, progress, egocentric goal bearing, and threshold crossing are graph-held assessments. The runner records them but never judges success.

rules.name: ea_choose_babble_action
rules.comment: Motor babble is chosen in graph space: least-sampled opaque actuator first, with external enumeration ordinal only as a stable tie break.

rules.name: ea_choose_change_recalibration
rules.comment: Prediction surprise opens a finite graph-held re-probing window. Choose the least recently observed opaque actuator; neither the fault schedule nor actuator anatomy is available.

rules.name: ea_choose_model_action
rules.comment: After every opaque actuator has been sampled, choose the one whose learned body-frame consequence best serves the active control regime. Ordinary two-step distance descent remains the default; a graph-held lack of measured progress recruits orientation for nonholonomic local minima. Receipt-backed bearing improvement, learned rest, and learned turn quantum replace any fixed escape horizon. No morphology, forward-axis, or actuator label is visible.

rules.name: ea_prepare_shared_motor_collapse_values
rules.comment: Map the existing body-specific planning cost onto each episode-scoped option; the shared core owns the actual collapse.

rules.name: ea_choose_adaptation_probe
rules.comment: Graph-native system-identification arm: apply the same round-robin opaque interventions in adaptive and frozen-plasticity graphs so prediction recovery is not confounded by action choice.

rules.name: ea_choose_no_learning_control
rules.comment: No-learning control: graph-native deterministic round-robin choice over opaque actuators. Python neither chooses nor learns.

rules.name: ea_choose_random_control
rules.comment: Random-like no-learning control: a graph-held deterministic hash selects over opaque actuator models. No host choice or model update.

rules.name: ea_choose_shuffled_model_control
rules.comment: Ablation after babbling: retain the learned model table and graph planner but circularly permute the model-to-opaque-token association. This isolates whether the learned causal mapping, rather than generic motion, drives navigation.

rules.name: ea_open_motor_trial
rules.comment: Materialise the chosen opaque actuator and its current prediction as a graph trial before the world is touched.

rules.name: ea_learn_forward_model
rules.comment: Receipt-backed transition updates the selected ActionModel in graph space. Initial exact sample means establish a slow prior; the adaptive mode then uses recency-weighted updates, prediction-error surprise, and a faster plasticity rate when consequences change.

rules.name: ea_close_no_learning_trial
rules.comment: Receipt closes a control trial but changes no ActionModel.

rules.name: ea_expose_motor_decision_option
rules.comment: Initialize each opaque ActionModel in the shared collapse vocabulary. The hard preparation rule projects the existing local forward-planning cost at each decision epoch.
